question.problem:
An angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane (measured in the usual way) has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={15}^{∘}.$ List, in ascending order, all the possible values of $\theta $ in the range ${0}^{∘}\le \theta <{360}^{∘}.$

In ascending order, $\theta $ can be equal to ${15}^{∘},$
{{field-1}}
${}^{∘},\,$
{{field-2}}
${}^{∘},$ and
$\,\,{345}^{∘},$
question.worked_solution:
Let's remind ourselves of the relationship between ${\theta }_{R}$ and $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/4891c7eea304bff2598ba5b19118951183b196eb4f2f4249573706b6625066e2.png)

Using ${\theta }_{R}={15}^{∘},$ let's calculate all possible values of $\theta .$

- If $\theta $ lies in the first quadrant, then $\theta ={\theta }_{R}={15}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the second quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}-{15}^{∘}={165}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}+{15}^{∘}={195}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the fourth quadrant, then $\theta ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={360}^{∘}-{15}^{∘}={345}^{∘}.$

Therefore, in ascending order, $\theta $ can be equal to ${15}^{∘},$ ${165}^{∘},$ ${195}^{∘},$ and ${345}^{∘}.$
